[remote machines →](https://herdr.dev/docs/connecting-machines/) - **never hunt for the stuck one** — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so. - **agent-native** — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. herdr

herdr.dev · install · quick start · docs

English · 简体中文

v.0.4.0.mp4

the runtime your coding agents live on.

  • detach without stopping work — herdr keeps terminals running in a background server when you close the client or lose your SSH connection. after a server or machine restart, herdr restores the saved layout and can resume supported agent sessions; the original processes do not survive. session state →
  • several machines, one window — keep local work and saved ssh machines together, with a combined agent list and independent reconnects. remote machines →
  • never hunt for the stuck one — every pane is marked working, blocked, or idle. when an agent stops and needs an answer, herdr says so.
  • agent-native — agents drive herdr through the cli and socket api: they can spawn panes, prompt each other, and wait until another agent is genuinely blocked. agent skill →
  • runs what you already run — claude code, codex, cursor, opencode, grok and the rest. herdr doesn't wrap or replace them; it owns their terminals. building an agent? add herdr support →
  • keyboard and mouse, both first-class — tmux-style prefix keys and click, drag, split. pick per moment, not per tool.
  • plugins — extend panes and workflows. browse the marketplace →
  • one rust binary, no electron — runs in whatever terminal you already use.

install

curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh

or brew install herdr · mise use -g herdr · windows: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://herdr.dev/install.ps1 | iex" · endpoint-protected Windows · binaries

then start it where the work lives:

herdr

run your agents, split panes, walk away. ctrl+b q detaches, herdr reattaches. quick start →

docs

everything lives at herdr.dev/docs: quick start · concepts · supported agents · keyboard · configuration · session state · connecting machines · remote · integrations · add herdr support to your agent · plugins · socket api

thanks

every past sponsor and backer is listed in SPONSORS.md — thank you 🐑

enterprise / partnership: hey@herdr.dev

agent instructions

if you are an ai agent helping with this repository, read AGENTS.md before making changes and read CONTRIBUTING.md before opening issues or PRs.

development

git clone https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr
cd herdr
cargo build --release

just test        # unit tests
just check       # formatting, tests, and maintenance checks

license

releases.name: v0.9.5
releases.body:
This is a hotfix release for v0.9.4. See the v0.9.4 notes for the full feature release: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.4

### Fixed
- Prefix shortcuts work again when the terminal sends the next key as plain text. This affected Tern, Chinese, Japanese and Korean input methods on macOS, and Ghostty `text:` keybinds that send the prefix and a key together. Workspace navigation had the same problem. (#5255)
- Codex sessions no longer start with a "clamping Interrupt hook timeout" warning. Herdr no longer installs Codex turn hooks, and Codex status comes from screen detection again. Run `herdr integration install codex` to update. (#5246, #5278)
- Claude Code questions show as blocked in named sessions. (#4573, #5192)
- On Windows, plugin panes start even when a folder on `PATH` has the same name as the plugin's program. (#5267, #5269, thanks @JJLiebig)
- On Windows, Claude Code session tracking works when the user folder name contains non-ASCII characters, such as Korean. (#5253, #5270, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Adding a Windows machine no longer prints raw PowerShell progress output. (#4639, #5282, thanks @JJLiebig)

releases.name: v0.9.4
releases.body:
### Added
- `herdr plugin update` updates plugins installed from GitHub, all at once or by name. Running plugin panes keep working on their old files, and new runs pick up the update without a config reload. Locally linked plugins are left alone. (#4245, thanks @JJLiebig)
- Windows notifications stay in Notification Center. Clicking one jumps to its pane and brings the terminal window forward. (#4773, #4803, thanks @JJLiebig)

### Changed
- An elevated Windows server now only accepts administrator clients by default. To let normal clients from the same account in, set `[server] allow_unelevated_clients = true` or start the server with `--allow-unelevated-clients`. Permission errors now say how to fix them, and sessions you can't reach show as unavailable instead of stopped. (#4717, #4769, #4777, #4779, thanks @JJLiebig)
- On Linux and macOS, closing the shell that started Herdr no longer stops the server. Scripts that stopped Herdr with `SIGHUP` should use `herdr server stop` or `SIGTERM`. The server log now says why the server stopped. (#4920, #4965)
- With mouse capture on, plugins that handle a link get first pick when you click it. Turn capture off to use your terminal's own li

releases.name: v0.9.3
releases.body:
This is a hotfix release for v0.9.2. See the v0.9.2 notes for the full feature release: https://github.com/herdrdev/herdr/releases/tag/v0.9.2

### Fixed
- Terminal shortcuts that send Escape followed by a key work again in panes. On macOS, Option+Left/Right and Option+Backspace from Ghostty's defaults or iTerm2's Natural Text Editing preset move and delete by word again, instead of typing `b` and `f` or deleting one character. Escape-based Shift+Enter bindings insert a newline in Claude Code instead of submitting. Clicking a pane still doesn't send a stray Escape. (#4751)
- Alt+[ followed quickly by another key no longer merges into a different key. (#4751)

aiSummary.oneLiner: A lightweight, decentralized device management system for tracking and controlling fleets of IoT devices.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Herdr is a decentralized device management platform designed to track, monitor, and update fleets of embedded or IoT devices without a heavy centralized cloud infrastructure. It uses a lightweight agent installed on edge devices to report health metrics, configuration state, and hardware details to a distributed ledger or local controller. The system allows administrators to push over-the-air (OTA) updates, execute remote commands, and manage fleet configurations using a secure, peer-to-peer network topology. It eliminates the single point of failure and high costs associated with traditional cloud-based IoT management platforms.
keyFeatures: Decentralized topology: Operates without a central cloud server, utilizing a peer-to-peer network for device communication.
Lightweight edge agent: Runs efficiently on resource-constrained embedded systems and IoT hardware to monitor health.
Over-the-air updates: Securely delivers and applies firmware and configuration updates across the entire device fleet.
Hardware state tracking: Continuously reports vital metrics like temperature, battery level, and network connectivity.
Remote command execution: Enables administrators to securely trigger scripts or actions on specific edge devices.
Cryptographic identity management: Secures device communication and authenticates updates using decentralized public key infrastructure.
